newsitem.title: SLOVAKIA: SLOVAK FINMIN CUTS MATURITY FOR FEB26 BOND AUCTION.
newsitem.headline: SLOVAK FINMIN CUTS MATURITY FOR FEB26 BOND AUCTION.

text.p: The Slovak Finance Ministry on Monday said it would auction an unspecified tranche of one- year state bonds on February 26, instead of the originally planned issue with a maturity of four years.

"We changed the maturity after a survey of the market. We think that a one-year bond has a better chance of success than the originally planned maturity," Marian Horvath, head of the ministry's State Assets and Liabilities Department, told Reuters.
The bonds will carry a fixed, 10.0 percent coupon paid semi-annually, and will have no limit price set on bids.
The ministry also changed the maturity of bonds at its first auction this year from four years to one year, and then rejected all bids in the auction.
The last successfull auction of one-year state bonds was October 17, when the ministry accepted bids totalling 2.179 billion crowns at an average yield of 9.16 percent.
Horvath would not comment on where the ministry planned to accept bids. "We want to give it (the one-year bond) another chance, that's all I can say at the moment," he said.
The Finance Ministry uses treasury bills and state bonds as the main source to cover the state budget deficit.

Slovakia showed a state budget surplus of 2.884 billion crowns in the first month of the year, but the overall 1997 state budget deficit is planned at 36.9 billion crowns, compared with a deficit of 25.5 billion crowns last year.
The government plans to issue 70 billion crowns worth of securities on the domestic market this year.
